Regulation: B.C. Reg. 112/2026
Made under: Budget Measures Implementation Act
Published in: No. 13 – B.C. Regs. 110 to 124, July 14, 2026
Deposit date: July 9, 2026

B.C. Reg. 112/2026, deposited July 9, 2026, under theBUDGET MEASURES IMPLEMENTATION ACT, 2026[section 103] andPROVINCIAL SALES TAX ACT[sections 236 and 241]. Order in Council 294/2026, approved and ordered July 9, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective February 18, 2026, the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation, B.C. Reg. 97/2013, is amended as set out in the attached Appendix. — B. BAILEY,Minister of Finance; A. DIX,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 26 of the Provincial Sales Tax Exemption and Refund Regulation, B.C. Reg. 97/2013, is amended (a)	by adding the following subsection: (1.1)	A purchaser who purchases tangible personal property at a sale in British Columbia is exempt from tax imposed under Part 3 of the Act if (a)	the purchaser purchased the tangible personal property for a business use, (b)	the tangible personal property is to be shipped by the purchaser for delivery outside British Columbia, and (c)	no use is to be made of the tangible personal property while the tangible personal property is in British Columbia other than storage of the tangible personal property., (b)	in subsection (2) by striking out "Subsection (1) of this section is prescribed" and substituting "Subsections (1) and (1.1) of this section are prescribed", and (c)	by adding the following subsection: (3)	For the purposes of section 145 (1.1) (a)[evidence required to claim certain exemptions in relation to tangible personal    property or software]of the Act, in relation to a purchaser who alleges that the tangible personal property is exempt under subsection (1.1) of this section, the collector is required to obtain a declaration, in a form specified by the director, that the tangible personal property is for a business use. minutes_briefs.title: PST exemption expanded for goods bought in BC and shipped out of province for business use
minutes_briefs.summary: British Columbia has expanded its Provincial Sales Tax (PST) exemption. Starting February 18, 2026, businesses can buy tangible personal property (physical goods like equipment or inventory) in BC without paying PST, as long as the goods are for business use and will be shipped out of the province. The goods cannot be used in BC—only stored here before shipping. To claim this exemption, the seller must get a signed declaration from the buyer confirming the goods are for business use.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you sell goods that will be shipped out of BC for business use, update your sales process to collect a signed business-use declaration from the buyer to claim the PST exemption.

key_dates.label: BC PST exemption for out-of-province business goods takes effect
